system.summary: Royalist numeric nomenclators (two-digit figures for letters, about 100 to 398 in 1645 and to 697 in 1646 for words) in five documents; f. 107 is a simple graphic-sign substitution with a few homophones (key f. 106).
system.sibling_key: Charles I-Rupert-Digby-Ormonde 1644-45 and Nicholas-Rupert July 1645 keys tested by range: do not fit
system.notes: Distinct symbols counted for the 1645 Maurice letter only (18 below 100, 45 above). f. 9 and f. 10 use different keys (f. 9 has no group above 343, f. 10 runs to 697). f. 107: about 20 graphic signs, m and n share ':'.

prior_solution.where: f. 107 (R8728) carries a partial contemporary interlinear gloss (on the image, found before the attempt); nothing in print or on DECODE for any of the six documents

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: trevor_anneal.py (homophonic annealing with cribs, lang en-1640s)

solution.what: Maurice's letter taken from the Warburton OCR; structure counted.
Known royalist key ranges compared with the 1645 figures.
Keys and originals located in BL Add MS 18980-82 and 72438; BL images offline since 2023, DECODE private.

DECODE cookie opens the private records; 115 records from Add MS 72438, 18982, 18983 listed with metadata (decode_records.tsv). No DOC transcriptions on any; Add MS 18980/18981 not on DECODE; no Maurice letter on DECODE.
f. 9r (R8623) and f. 10r-v (R8624) transcribed from the images: f. 9 letters 3-81 and words 100-343; f. 10 letters 1-99 and words 100-697; the two use different keys.
f. 25r (R8627) read: index of the keys taken in Digby's coach, numbered 80-139 with correspondents.

All 73 key records of Add MS 72438 screened by number range and structure from the images; most excluded by range (word series ending below 343, letter+digit codes, French/Latin/Weckherlin keys, 4-digit code).

Letter tables transcribed and applied to the letter runs of f. 9 and f. 10: key 118 Ormond-Rupert (R8655), key 123 King-Queen (R8687), key 125 Mr Browne (R8694), Digby-Walsingham (R8724), the 'To decypher speedily' key (R8744/R8745). All give gibberish.

Maurice 1645 tested against key 118 (Ormond-Rupert) letter table: '15 26 ... 13' = a m ... c, no sense; Tomokiyo's Nicholas-Rupert May 1645 key fragment (DECODE R8430/R8432 notes) gives no sense on Maurice or f. 9.

Add MS 18982 ff. 51-52 (R8433, 'Bristoll', non-decrypted) identified as Arthur Trevor to Rupert, Bristol 8 April 1645, with ~60 cipher groups of the same shape as Maurice's (letters <100, words 100+): a possible same-family key, not yet broken.
R8433 (Trevor to Rupert, Bristol [28] April 1645) cipher passages transcribed: 62 groups, 54 letter groups in 4 runs, 8 word groups.
Warburton iii OCR grepped for Trevor's April 1645 letter and the Molyneux/O'Neill passage; web search on the landing.
Homophonic annealing (en-1640s) on R8433's letter runs with 'chester'/'bristol' fixed on the 7-letter run and with no crib; box letter tables applied.
f. 104r (R8725) transcribed: 253 numeric groups + endorsement 347 313 364; no decipherment on the sheet despite DECODE 'Decrypted'.

f. 104 tested with letter tables 118, 123, 125, R8744 and the Parliament key R8741 (letters 10-72, nulls 1-9/73-75): nonsense. f. 107 (R8728) is a graphic cipher, so its key cannot apply to f. 9/f. 10.
f. 106 (R8727) two graphic alphabets transcribed; the lower one tested on f. 107 (R8728) against the interlinear gloss ('I hoped for some comfortable lynes ...').

f. 107 deciphered line by line with the f. 106 lower alphabet plus a few unlisted homophones (Ʈ=h, ɣ=r, 7=y, plain e, plain α=t): 129 words, 6 unread = 95.3%. A woman's letter to a royalist officer who got safe to the King; no names or date.

Write-up count: f107_reading.txt measured (129 tokens less the editorial '[one]' = 128 cipher words, 122 read = 95.3%); line 6 transcribed sign by sign and decoded with the f. 106 lower alphabet (f107_decode.py) for the reveal; all six documents measured for fraction_read.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): f. 107: reading f107_reading.txt, sign transcription only of line 6 (f107_decode.py); the five undeciphered documents listed with their transcriptions and no decryption

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the five numeric documents carry no state and so counted as read by default; each is an undeciphered ciphertext and is now marked decoded, not read. Claim unchanged (fraction_read already counts them at 0).

Reading audit b10: George Lasry's reconstructed keys of the sibling King/Queen 1645-46 targets (TNA SP 106, SP106-2, SP106-3, SP106-5 that read rupert1645, SP106-8), fetched from DECODE R785, R787, R929, R924 and goring1645, applied to all five numeric documents. f. 104 reads as English with SP106-8 (201 of 256 groups get a value; endorsement 347 313 364 = The King to the Prince of Wales); Maurice 1645, f. 9, f. 10 and Trevor 1645 give gibberish under all five.
Printed text of the f. 104 letter looked for: Clarendon State Papers ii (1773) and Bruce, Charles I in 1646 (1856) grepped on archive.org, two web searches; Petrie 1935 lending-only. Nothing found.

f. 104 transcription checked on the full-resolution image (no label changed); key gaps filled from Lasry's own interlinear of R924 (3, 7, 12, 30, 50 word spaces; 116 = can, not BROUGHT; 127 do, 207 may, 208 made, 320 upon, 334 what, 450 command, 513 express) and from the letter's contexts (f104_key_additions.tsv, f104_decode.py); reading built and aligned word by word (f104_reading.md, f104_en.md, f104_reread_log.md). Body scores 0.267 (4/15 sentences); 21 nomenclator groups have no key material, so it stays decoded, not read.

Verify sweep (reading audit v2): f. 107 reading re-checked line by line on the DECODE image IMG_R8728_I40333_P1 against the f. 106 lower alphabet and the contemporary interlinear gloss. Two words partly carried and now bracketed in f107_reading.txt: 'one another' is written o-n-a-t-h-e-r, 'should' ends in the c sign. Reading body scored with every conjecture, supplied or partly carried word as an explicit hole (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py): 0.273 on the modern word list (1640s spelling: lynes, ioyfull, neuer, sattisfied), 0.818 on explicit holes (9 of 11 sentences); the sentences hold for a reader. Kept read.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Issue #554 (aaymeloglu): f. 10 identified as Digby-cabinet key no. 129 (f. 25r index; surviving page f. 77, R8701, names 559-580) from 562 Davenant / 572 Mylord in f. 10 and the word values of Charles I's 1646 letters to Nicholas printed with their decipherment (Evelyn iv. 178-179). Checked here: the Evelyn values against the archive.org text; contributor's f. 10 transcription vs this folder's (685 of ~720 groups agree); own script aaymeloglu_f10/apply_key129.py: 190 of 715 groups take a value, fragments only.

outcome.method_basis: The only text obtained is f. 107 (R8728), deciphered 95.3% of words with the lower alphabet of the key sheet filed beside it (f. 106, R8727); the cryptiana items themselves (Maurice 1645, f. 9, f. 10) and R8433 are not solved, so the primary method describes a by-product of the search, not the targets as posed. f. 104 (R8725), Charles I to the Prince of Wales, was matched on 22 Oct 2026 to George Lasry's key TNA SP106-8 and deciphered in part (decoded, not read: 4 of 15 sentences hold).
outcome.notes: Read in part only through f. 107, a letter found beside the targets in the same volume. The cryptiana items #5 and #6 remain unread: f. 9/f. 10 are May 1646, seven months after the coach keys were taken (Oct 1645), so their keys were probably never captured with them; Maurice's 'your cipher' is not in the volume or on DECODE.

outcome.fraction_read_source: All six documents, cipher tokens, clear words excluded: maurice1645_groups.txt 93 groups, f9_groups.txt 152, f10_groups.txt 721, f104_groups.txt 256 (with the endorsement), trevor1645_transcription.txt 62 (--digits), f107_reading.txt 128 cipher words (129 with --drop-first, less the editorial '[one]'); total 1,412. Read: 122 words of f. 107 ([..?] conjectures counted unread); the numeric documents 0. 122/1412 = 0.086. f. 107 is counted in words, not signs, because no full sign-level transcription exists; counted in letters it would weigh about four times more, so the figure is a lower bound of the share of cipher material read, and the cryptiana items themselves stand at 0. 22 Oct 2026 (reading audit b10): f. 104 is deciphered in part with Lasry's SP106-8 but does not read (0.267 of sentences clean), so it stays at 0; no document changed state, fraction_read unchanged at 122/1412.

texts.label: BL Add MS 72438 f. 107r (DECODE R8728)
texts.summary: A woman's graphic-sign letter in English to a royalist officer: she had heard he was killed or taken, rejoices that he got safe to the King, and reproaches him for neglect after so many years' acquaintance. Deciphered with the lower alphabet of the neighbouring key sheet f. 106 (R8727), checked against the partial interlinear gloss; 122 of 128 words. Only line 6 is transcribed sign by sign (in f107_decode.py).
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.1% of the words of f107_reading.txt read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

Not deciphered: the file is the ciphertext (numeric groups from Warburton iii. 133). No key fits: the 73 keys of Add MS 72438 (9 Oct) and, on 22 Oct 2026 (reading audit b10), George Lasry's five reconstructed SP 106 keys of the King/Queen 1645-46 siblings (SP 106, SP106-2, -3, -5, -8) give gibberish. Blocker: no-key-material (Rupert's cipher to his brother is not known).

texts.label: BL Add MS 18982 ff. 51-52 (DECODE R8433), [28] Apr 1645
texts.summary: Arthur Trevor to Prince Rupert from Bristol, mostly clear (Sir Vivian Molineux, Sir Bryan O'Neile, the Prince of Wales's journey westward) with short numerical cipher passages; not deciphered.

texts.note: Deciphered in part, not read (reading audit b10, 22 Oct 2026): the letter is in George Lasry's key TNA SP106-8 (DECODE R924); with his key unchanged plus 35 values from his R924 interlinear and the letter's own contexts (f104_key_additions.tsv) the body scores 0.267 (4 of 15 sentences clean). The command to the Prince and the 'let the Queen be judge whether I really send for you' clause hold; the opening line and 21 nomenclator groups (466, 543, 534, 668, 643, 502, 769 ...) are absent from R924 or unidentified there: no key material. Partial reading kept in f104_reading.md.
texts.label: BL Add MS 72438 f. 104r (DECODE R8725)
texts.summary: Charles I to the Prince of Wales (the endorsement '347 313 364' decodes as 'The King to the Prince of Wales'), a clerk's all-numeric fair copy, undated [1646?]: the King is content that the Prince has been referred to the Queen, and lays a command on him that no persuasion or threatening whatsoever make him [come into England?] before his father sends for him; a summons he has not really sent is to be judged by the Queen. Deciphered in part with George Lasry's key 'TNA SP106-8' (DECODE R924) and 35 values from R924's interlinear and this letter's contexts.
